notes.text: 1) buyer.talks.none_in_stock counts OTHER shops answering our buyer 'none in stock'; it is not our shop's stock. Our sku_depth/window_depth do not change it; raise them only for our own stock-outs (our shop's lost asks in demand). 2) FOOD_MARGIN: the 57 shelf-life refusals were mostly before the buyer began reading the shop's stated hours and leaving before a deal (11/3 21:20); in our last 60 payments only 2 were refused for shelf life. Each step up asks shops for longer shelf life than the order needs, so fewer shops can serve it. 1.1-1.15 looks enough; raise it only if shelf-life refusals in payments rise again.

Revenue is our weakest shop term (0.545) and you found every lever flat for 10 cycles. The market's revenue is ~85% furniture/bedding (24 h ledger: 622M of 730M), and our max_list 80000 and goods_frac 0.25 keep us out of most of it. The ledger's last 24 h of 가구/침구 settles by list price: under 80k 1508 sold at 0.74 of list, broke 3.9%; 80-150k 636 at 0.75, broke 3.6%; 150-450k 1944 at 0.75, broke 3.3%. Dearer units sell as often, at the same share of list, and break no more. Suggest one step at a time: max_list up (e.g. 130000), goods_frac up one step, keeping reserve_cash; then watch sell-through of the dearer units, storage days and refunds for two or three cycles before the next step. Your call.

max_list: the score rise from 0.788 to 0.811 did not come from it. Since 11:08 (max_list 130000) only 2 of our talks were for units listed above 80000 (both sold, 125,002 revenue), and 1 such unit is in stock now; the new stock arrives only in supply windows. Hold max_list at 230000 until dearer units have been bought and had time to sell (two or three supply windows), then judge by their sell-through, days in storage and refunds, not by the score of the next cycle.

Revenue is our weakest shop term (pct 0.60; the top shop sold 274M against our 31M, mostly furniture). We hold 13.2M in cash and only 1.1M of stock at cost, while goods_frac 0.45 of stock_value 2.5M leaves about 1.1M for goods, about seven mattresses. 103 of the last 865 asks to our shop (12%) found nothing in stock. stock_value may now go up to 8,000,000 (750,000 a cycle). Suggest raising it step by step while dearer goods keep selling within a few supply windows; keep reserve_cash, and watch unsold days and refunds.

Where the money is (24 h ledger): dae-yangkim made 57M profit from 284 settles, 99% goods (침대/매트리스 157, 침구 98, 소파 27), average ticket 459,240, paid 0.86 of list; dragonash 344 settles, average 248,424; we sold 511 at an average of 27,780 and none at 150,000 or more. A mattress at 0.86 of list leaves about 30% of list over cost, more than a hundred food sales. max_list may now go to 1,500,000 (100,000 a cycle) and goods_frac to 0.8; with 13M cash idle, suggest stepping max_list, goods_frac and stock_value up together each cycle while the dear goods sell within a few supply windows, and holding goods asks near the market's 0.75-0.86 rather than cutting them.

The user (11/4 13:00) found our list-price cap too conservative and set max_list 600000, goods_frac 0.6, stock_value 5,000,000 (from {'max_list': 330000, 'goods_frac': 0.55, 'stock_value': 3250000}). Keep them unless the dear goods fail to sell within a few supply windows; the steps are now 200,000 for max_list and 1,000,000 for stock_value, so you can follow quickly either way.

Mattresses sell out within minutes: 13:04 window bought K 388,153, LK 459,929 and Q 150,989 (one each); the K sold at 446,430 at 13:07 and all three were gone before 13:24. The 13:24 window again bought one LK and one Q, after twelve bed pads, kimchi and apples took the first lines; the LK sold at once. Dear goods get qty 1 because their category score is still low in our own sales. Suggest dear_first up to 3 and depth up, so each window buys 3-5 mattresses first, while they keep selling within the window gap (20 min); cash is 13.1M, stock 2.0M at cost.

Board 14:40: rank 20/51, total 1.234 = shop 0.725 + buyer 0.509. The buyer side is the gap: top-6 buyers score 0.76-0.91. We close 771 deals of 1980 orders (39%); they close 50-65% (inextro 1523/2610, kimauve 1324/2030) and their surplus is 31-80M against our 11.1M. Their paid ratio is not lower than ours on average (0.50-0.69 vs our 0.583), so they win by closing more orders, including dear ones, not by squeezing harder. In the last 400 buyer lines many orders end dropped/rejected by the same shops (G476cc094 at shaun0927, yeonsong2, jiseokkk). Please look at why orders go unserved (too-low opens, MAX_TRIES, CAP, shops we keep retrying) and lift the deal rate; a closed deal at modest surplus beats a dropped one.

FOOD_MARGIN went 1.15 -> 1.2 at 15:27. A higher margin cannot cut the shelf-life refusals: the units shops shipped had 114-375 h left against 207-621 h asked, short even at margin 1.0; each raise only makes the kit refuse units that would last and shrinks the food we can buy. From 15:29 the buyer remembers a shop/SKU that shipped a short unit and tries it last for an hour on orders needing more hours (avoid_r3.json), and pairs that answered none-in-stock wait 15 min; a second scout wave asks new shops when the first wave is all out. Suggest FOOD_MARGIN back to 1.1 and judging the refusal count after an hour of the new memory.

Goal: top 10 (now 17th, 1.272; 10th is 1.44). Buyer ALL = surplus 0.5, forum votes 0.3, deals 0.1, posts 0.1; surplus = list price - price paid. In the ledger window, top buyers settle a SKU listed at 200k or more on 20-46% of their orders (inextro 426 of 935, mjforge 234 of 733); we do on 4% (25 of 622). They pay 0.69-0.76 of list, more than our 0.67, on far dearer SKUs: our surplus per deal is 19k against 41-162k. An order's acceptable SKUs are priced 0.5-1.5x a reference and the budget is about 1.15x it, so the dearest acceptable SKU that a shop sells at about 0.75 of list still fits the budget; our talks pick SKUs listed at a median 0.85 of the budget. Please find why the buyer does not reach for the dearest acceptable SKU that fits (candidate scoring, the scouts' value at the shop's opening ask, CAP) and propose the fix as a code idea; a 300k-list deal at 0.75 is worth ten of our usual ones.

warranty_hours went 4 -> 6 at 18:30 and back to 6 -> 4 at 18:46 on one cycle's profit and rank. A 15-minute profit dip is mostly restock buying (cash into stock), and rank moves with everyone else; neither can see a warranty that covers grade-A goods only (1.4% break, so 6 h costs about 1.4% of those prices). By the board's weights stars cost us the fewest shop points (0.06; profit 0.13, revenue 0.11). Please hold a warranty change at least an hour and judge it on settles and refunds, not on one cycle; flipping a number back and forth teaches nothing.

Supervisor set CAP back 0.80 -> 0.85 at 21:20. In the last 6 h, 29 of our 538 deals were paid at 0.80-0.85 of list and brought 720,612 of surplus (6% of the 12.07M total); CAP 0.80 makes all of those no-deals, which earn 0, unless shops start conceding below 0.80, which nothing in the traces shows. Surplus is summed over deals: losing affordable deals lowers it. The user (11/4): our buyer and seller are both too strict. A lower CAP needs an A/B or evidence that shops concede, not one step on thin evidence.

The shop's money is in dear furniture and we barely sell it. Last 6 h of settles: inextro 730M from 575 units listed at 150k+ (386 sofas), dae-yangkim 543M, gom31 428M; we sold 25 such units, 21M of revenue, average ticket 41k, with 21M cash idle and 2.6M of stock at cost. From 22:40 restock buys up to 18 lines a window and 4 units of each dear SKU (dear_depth, lines: merchandising's knobs), and stock_value is 12M (bound now 20M). Please keep stock flowing into sofas, beds and bedding that are not surged; judge on shop margin and revenue per hour over two hours, not one cycle; raise stock_value further while dear units keep selling within the window gap.

Two corrections about the shop's A/B test. 1) The 150-order minimum is for the buyer's and the code's trials (orders split by hash), not for the shop's A/B, which counts negotiations and ends at p_win, or as a tie after 250 talks an arm or 2 h. Its arm B had only 18 talks against 208 because the draw leaned after 10; from 23:05 both arms get min_n (30) first. 2) A running A/B does not freeze the shop: changing a number that is NOT on test applies to both arms alike and does not confound the result. Keep moving the other numbers (stock, ask/floor for the other kind, warranty) on their own evidence while a test runs.

Dear stock works: since the 22:44 restock (20 mattresses, 4 bed frames) we sold 59 units listed at 100k+ in one hour, against about 4 an hour before; cash went 8.6M -> 13.1M while stock is 10.9M at cost (book 24M, +5M). Stock was at the 12M cap, so the supervisor set stock_value 16M at 23:55. Merchandising: keep raising it a step at a time while dear units keep selling within the window gap, and lower it the cycle they stop.

Market rules changed 11/5 03:49: the shop's first ALL term (weight 0.5) is now BOOK = cash + what unsold units cost, not cash. Buying stock no longer lowers our score until it sells; what costs us is stock that never sells: food past its date leaves the book at its cost, and goods pay storage while they wait. So: keep stocking dear goods that sell (furniture, bedding), keep food to what sells before its date, and judge stock_value by sell-through and spoilage, not by the cash dip after a restock.

clear_hours went 12 -> 16 at 03:51 and back 16 -> 12 at 04:07, the second flip-flop of the night (warranty 4 -> 6 -> 4 at 18:30/18:46). A number changed and undone 16 minutes later was never measured. Hold a change at least an hour (or put it on the A/B), then judge it on what it is about: for clear_hours, food units that expire unsold and the margin of clearance sales.

Playbook A/Bs keep being turned down for lack of a 'clean baseline'. An A/B does not need one: both arms run at the same hours under every other setting alike, so earlier flips, warranty or clear_hours changes affect both arms equally and cannot bias the comparison. The only real limit is the single slot. When the running test ends, put a goods playbook on it (IKEA or Costco: our goods are now most of the revenue), since a whole playbook is the biggest step the A/B can test and none has run yet.

Why deals fell after 08:00 (shop deals 190 -> 120 an hour while the market's settles rose 2,600 -> 2,850): not price but breadth. Our 291 units sat in 8 of 140 categories (four blankets 22-24 deep, one mattress 24 deep), and buyers only visit shops that hold the ordered category: talks with us fell from 350 to 250 an hour. From 10:10 restock gives its first breadth_lines (6) lines to categories we hold none of, and caps a cheap SKU at sku_cap (8) units; both are merchandising's knobs. Cutting the food ask treats a symptom; watch talks per hour and categories held.

Where the buyer's points are (11/3 21:00-11/5 11:00, 4,662 orders). 1) Orders with a reference price of 300k or more are 5% of orders (216) but gave 55% of our surplus (34.6M of 62.6M), closing 61%; 100-300k orders (281) close only 51%. Each dear order missed costs about 260k, about ten cheap deals; cheap orders under 30k (2,333) gave 15%. So effort per order should scale with the price: for dear orders scout every shop that has the SKU, keep talking, take a fair ask within budget; new metric buyer_dear_close (ref >= 100k). 2) The market sends the next order no sooner than 20 s after our answer; 31% of orders took longer (no-deal median 23 s, p90 66 s), so we get about 139 orders an hour where 170 are possible. For cheap orders that are going nowhere, leave sooner; new metric buyer_secs_order (lower is better), with buyer_paid_h as the guard. 3) Forum is a cumulative share (ours 0.584, top 0.60-0.63); recent posts get about 6 likes to 1 dislike, so every liked post lifts it, every disliked one costs; posts count only 0.1.

stock_value was the ceiling on dear goods: goods get goods_frac x stock_value and already held ~11M of 14.4M, so a window could add only ~3M of 150k+ goods, though they are 63% of our revenue (last 3 h). The top shops hold 50-150M of stock (Kiro729 51.6M at 297k a unit, revenue 1.30B vs our 235M). Stock counts in book at cost, so more stock does not lower book, only adds 1%/day storage. Supervisor set stock_value 30M and widened the bound to 50M. Next: watch dear units held, dear sales an hour and revenue for 2-3 cycles; if dear stock sells, step stock_value up; if it sits for over a day, step down. Add 500k+ SKUs (beds, sofas) where the ledger shows them settling.

Undid market_ask 1.05 -> 1.0. 12:34 market_ask 1.0 -> 1.05 came 30 min after stock_value 18M -> 30M (12:03), whose 2-3 cycle check the merchandiser asked for at 12:19; a price step now confounds it. Counted for the engineer (it cannot run scripts): the buyer's talks in market-kit.log 11/5 01:11-15:45, split at each CHOOSE (its 'paying at most' is our cap) and ended at OUT. 1,708 talks, 1,424 closed. Market outages, not our prices: on 11/5 the market's /api/shops came back empty from 16:12 to 16:45 and again around 17:16 (the kit logs 'no shops in the market yet'), so buyers could not find shops and our deals fell to 16-32 an hour in those 15-minute windows. Two changes to how numbers are judged (18:45). 1) Every shop number you change is now judged by code 2 h later: margin and deals an hour, 2 h before vs 2 h after, written to the ledger as source 'inner loop (number)', with any other number changed meanwhile named as a confound. So you need not hold every other number while one is judged; change one number a cycle and read its verdict when it comes. 2) The metrics now leave out the minutes the market listed no shops (outage_min). Correction to my 17:2x note: the kit's 'no shops' lines put the outage at 16:12-16:19, a moment at 16:26, 16:44-16:45, 17:06, 17:12, 17:16, 17:36 and 17:48 (about 15 minutes in all), not 16:12-16:45 whole.

Two misreadings: the 23:28 change was 16 -> 20, not 24 -> 20, and the 'profit' it read was cash, which falls whenever restock buys stock (stock at cost went 24.9M -> 29.6M in that hour while book stayed about 79M). RULES CHANGED 11/6 06:02 (agent.md). Buyer ALL now uses saved, not surplus: the sum over deals of (list - price) / list, a deal that served nothing (goods broke, food did not last) counting -1 (0 if refunded), divided by deals + 100. A snack and a sofa at 30% off score the same. Board at 06:0x: we are 9th of the Players (1.496); our saved 0.281 against a median 0.230 and max 0.364, buyer ALL 0.84; forum 0.887. What this means for the buyer: a deeper discount on every order counts, cheap orders count as much as dear ones, and a unit that breaks or spoils costs a whole deal's worth (C-grade goods broke 15.4% a day, A 1.5%), so C_CAP, grade and shelf-life rules now matter more than closing dear orders. Buyer trials are now judged on buyer_saved_deal (mean (list - price) / list per paid deal). Forum: votes count from voters with 50 settled deals, one stance per account per author; dislikes past 3 an hour cost the voter from 12:00. The shop side (book, revenue, stars) is unchanged and is now our weaker half (shop ALL 0.656).

08:05 board: we are 8th (1.504), tied with 9th, 0.04 behind 7th. Points lost now: shop book 0.132, shop revenue 0.091, then buyer posts 0.051, buyer saved 0.049 (we are at the 90th percentile there). The shop is where the points are, and every shop number has held since 03:11 (five hours). The verdicts you were waiting for are in: ask_frac 0.93 -61% (back to 0.9), clear_hours and sku_cap confounded but not harmful. Holding is itself a choice with a cost; take one shop number a cycle toward revenue and book, and let the 2 h verdict judge it. Revenue is mostly 300k+ furniture (about 5-19 sold an hour at 84-95k margin each) and cash sits at 60M: stock room for dear goods (stock_value 30M, now 23.9M held) and the dear ask are the levers with the most money behind them.

Undid dear_first to 3.0. 10:01 merchandising lowered dear_first 3.0 -> 2.5 citing my 08:0x note (one shop number a cycle toward revenue and book). That goes the other way: dear_first ranks 150k+ goods first in each supply window, and 300k+ furniture is most of our revenue (84-95k margin a unit), so less priority there means less revenue. It also stacked a third change on max_list (due 10:25) and sku_cap (due 10:41), which the same cycle's sales rejected as confounding. Back to 3.0. My note meant: move a number that adds revenue, one at a time, once the pending verdicts are in.

Market ledger 06:40-12:40: 4,379 units of 300k+ settled (4.31B won) across 54 shops; we sold 6. We held none of the 12 best sellers (지누스 그린티 매트리스 429 sold, 자코모 소파 447, 에이스침대 337, 시몬스 299...) and 24 units of a SKU that sold 11. Two causes in restock_r3.py: (1) priorities had grown to the thousands once settles fed sku_score, so dear_first's bonus (at most +9) changed nothing and cheap lines took the window; (2) a best seller planned 20 units (2.5-28M at cost), more than the goods room, and was skipped. Fixed: dear priority is a factor (1 + dear), dear lines are bought at their depth trimmed to the room. And the room itself: goods held 23.3M of 25.6M (goods_frac 0.8 x 32M) with 60M cash idle, so stock_value 32M -> 40M (book counts stock at cost). Watch 300k+ units bought per window and sold an hour; if the best sellers sell, keep stock_value up; the old slow dear stock (Gf918c335 x24) can clear through the aged-goods rule.

13:24 window bought 1 unit of the market's best seller (지누스 매트리스, 416 sold in 6 h) because goods held 31.7M of 32.0M (goods_frac 0.8 x 40M); food is only 2.8M of stock. 13.9M of it is goods older than 12 h (133 units: 20 x a 195k SKU, 15 x a 499k one) that the aged rule clears only after 5 days. goods_frac 0.8 -> 0.9 (bound up to 0.95), goods_age_days 5 -> 2 so slow goods sell down and free room.

13:44 window: breadth lines bought 2 gaming PCs and an air purifier (3.2M) before the market's best seller, which got 1 unit. Fixed in restock_r3.py: best-selling 300k+ SKUs (sku_score >= DEAR_HOT 200) go first, breadth lines take no other 150k+ goods. After that the binding limit is stock_value: stock 37.9M of 40M (2.1M of spend) with 49M cash idle, while the market's 15 best-selling 300k+ SKUs sold 100-450 units each in 6 h. stock_value 40M -> 50M (the bound); goods_age_days 2 clears slow goods into cash. If the best sellers do not sell within a day, bring stock_value back down.

Reverted 349ada8 (300k+ stock capped by our own past sales): reverted by the supervisor at 14:4x: it caps 300k+ stock at 4 h of OUR OWN 300k+ sales (2.2 an hour), but those were low because until 12:46 restock never bought the market's best sellers (a ranking and room bug, fixed 12:46-13:48); the market sold 4,379 units of 300k+ in 6 h, and the first window with the fix (14:02) sold 3 of them within 30 min.
